Coverage and model runs for each taxonomic group in the current release. Groups are added one at a time.

title: About
text: This resource is built and maintained by the Data Diversity Lab at the University of Arizona.

title: About
text:
The gap this fills
Several studies have shown that machine learning can assign provisional risk categories to unassessed and Data Deficient species, with accuracies close to expert assessment for the threatened and non threatened distinction. Each of those studies released its predictions as supplementary material for one taxonomic group at one point in time.

Relationship to IUCN

title: Methods
text: Each prediction is the output of a model trained on species that already have IUCN assessments, applied to species that do not. The methods come from published work, principally IUCNN. We did not develop a new method.

title: Methods
text:
What a probability means
prob_threatened is the model’s estimate that a species would fall into a threatened category if it were formally assessed. It is not a probability of extinction, and it is not a substitute for the criteria IUCN applies.

title: Methods
text:
Why several predictions per species
A species may be run through more than one model, and models are re run as data improve. We keep results for every run is kept. The species page shows all of them rather than one. We think that agreement between independent runs is information on its own. Yet, the consensus figure is the median across runs. The spread is the standard deviation.

title: Methods
text:
Training and evaluation
Models are trained on assessed species and evaluated with spatially blocked cross validation rather than a random split. Species that occur near each other share climate, sampling effort, and often conservation status, so a random split lets information pass between training and test data and inflates the apparent accuracy.
Performance is reported separately for threatened and non threatened species.

title: Methods
text:
Versioning
Predictions are never edited in place. A new release adds new files and the previous release stays available. The changelog records what moved.

title: Methods
text:
Limits worth knowing
Predictions rest on occurrence data, and occurrence data reflects where people have looked as much as where species are. Poorly sampled regions and poorly collected taxa carry more uncertainty than the probability alone suggests.
These estimates are meant to direct assessment effort and research attention.

title: Predicted extinction risk
text:
Everything on this site is a provisional, model based estimate. None of it is an IUCN assessment, and none of it should be cited as a species’ conservation status.
Many described species have never been evaluated for the IUCN Red List, and many of those that have been evaluated are listed as Data Deficient. Data Deficient does not mean a species is safe. It means the evidence was not enough to decide. Species in that position are generally left out of conservation planning for reasons that have nothing to do with their actual risk.
This site holds model based predictions of extinction risk for those species. The methods come from published work, principally IUCNN.

title: Predicted extinction risk
text:
How to use this
The priority list ranks species by how likely the models think they are to be threatened.
Browse filters the whole database. Groups reports how each model performed on species that do have assessments.
Each species page shows every prediction made for that species. We highlight instances where models disagree.

title: Downloads
text:
The site data
The JSON the site reads is served alongside it, so it works as an API without any further setup.
data/index.json holds one entry per species, with the consensus prediction.
data/species/<id>.json holds the full record for one species, including every prediction made for it.
data/groups.json and data/release.json hold coverage and release metadata.

title: Downloads
text:
Citing a release
Cite the release you used, not the site in general. Predictions change between releases, and a citation without a version cannot be checked later.
Each release is archived with a DOI at [TBD].

title: Downloads
text:
What is not here
No IUCN Red List data is stored or served by this site. Assessments, categories, narratives, threat codes, and range polygons are available within the IUCN.
